description: Tutorial lesson T3 (Get Movin'), mouse+keyboard player path: menu -> picker -> lesson boots from tutorial_postdeploy -> disembark the Boyz+Warboss from the Battlewagon via the real row-click + ConfirmationDialog + 11 placement clicks inside the 3-inch ring -> the boyz_move_after_disembark step teaches that the disembarked unit still gets its own move because the wagon has not moved yet, AND reminds the player they can grab all 11 at once: the card is asserted to name Ctrl+A, the shortcut is pressed for real, every alive Boy plus the attached Warboss is asserted selected in MULTI mode, and the drag off one selected model is asserted to stage more than one model (End This Unit's Move) -> Advance the Battlewagon through the mode radio + Confirm Movement Mode gate -> move the hull in TWO drags (asserting the second adds to the first, which is what the step now tells the player) -> turn it with Q held mid-drag on the 'POINT IT RIGHT!' step -> End This Unit's Move -> End Movement Phase under a strict spotlight -> summary, completion persisted, back to menu.

steps.comment: OK on the native ConfirmationDialog - its internal button has no scene path for click_node
19.03: the attached Warboss disembarks WITH the Boyz. Before the fix the placement only asked for the 10 Boyz, reported complete, and left the Warboss aboard.
The Warboss model is actually ON THE BOARD at a placed position, not merely flagged as disembarked
Battlewagon is empty — neither the Boyz nor the Warboss are left inside
11e 18.04 - a tactical disembark from a transport that has NOT moved leaves the unit selected to make its own move; the new step teaches that affordance

the step must REMIND the player they can grab the whole mob at once - 11 models dragged one at a time is the slow path players fall into right after a disembark. {key:select_all} renders through KeybindingManager, so this also proves the token resolved (an unresolved token would read '{key:select_all}').
the shortcut the card now advertises

the card's claim driven for real: Ctrl+A grabbed every alive Boy AND the attached Warboss (MovementController._select_all_unit_models walks the bodyguard plus attached characters), which is the 'all 11' the prompt promises
selecting the mob is not moving it - the step must not advance on a selection

m1 is at board (480,500) after placement - dragging a SELECTED model shifts the WHOLE formation 40px (1") (MovementController._start_group_movement), well inside the 6" cap and coherency. Away from the wagon, not towards it: the Battlewagon hull spans board x 561-719 / y 178-462, so a 1" step towards it puts the middle of the front rank inside the hull and only the two outer Boyz can be placed.
staging a model must NOT advance the step - it waits for the move to be locked in
the Boy really moved - guards against a zero-distance stage passing for a move (staged moves only reach GameState on CONFIRM_UNIT_MOVE, so this reads the live move data)

Let the group-drop staging pipeline drain before counting. MovementController._end_group_drag emits one STAGE_MODEL_MOVE per model with a 0.01s gap, then waits 0.1s and re-sends any straggler - for an 11-model mob that is ~2s of real time once each action's phase processing is included. The group_drop_in_flight assertion below is the actual gate; this wait just gets us there.

The staging batch has finished. Without this gate the all-11 assertion below can read model_distances mid-batch and report the last models as 'did not move' when they stage a frame later - a false failure that says nothing about the feature.

'one drag shifts da whole mob' proven end to end: ONE drag off ONE selected model staged real distance for EVERY alive Boy and the attached Warboss. This is also the regression pin for the group-drag key collision - group_drag_start_positions used to be keyed by bare model_id, so the Warboss ('m1') inherited the first Boy's start position, was sent to the BOY's destination, and the phase rejected it as 'Distance 7.5" exceeds cap 6.0"'. He never moved, and the two Boyz whose destinations he was still standing in were blocked behind him - 8 of 11 placed instead of 11.
confirming the move wrote the new position through to GameState

REPORTED BUG ('it says tutorial_locked when I select Advance'): MovementController._on_confirm_mode_pressed emits BEGIN_ADVANCE and then LOCK_MOVEMENT_MODE from ONE click, and BEGIN_ADVANCE completes wagon_mode synchronously (phase_action_taken -> _check_done -> _advance_step). So the second half of that click is gated by keep_da_roll's allow-list, which was empty - the mode never locked and the player got a red 'tutorial_locked'. mode_locked is the observable proof the lock landed.
and the gate itself allows it - so a re-confirm cannot resurrect the toast

the dice popups must be entirely the player's — an injected 'Exit Tutorial' lands in the AcceptDialog's own button bar, which is a separate focus root from its content, and on a pad that took Keep Roll / Re-roll away from the D-pad entirely. Same dialog class the charge roll uses.
Keep Roll lives inside an embedded Window (AcceptDialog) - real-coordinate clicks into embedded windows are unreliable, the schema's emit_pressed escape hatch exists for this

steps.script:
var o = tree.root.get_node("/root/TutorialOverlay")
return o.current_body_text().contains("grab it again")
steps.comment: the card must actually SAY the move can be spent over several drags - players were treating the drag as one-shot and burning the whole move by accident
first hop - deliberately only part of the way, the second drag below proves the rest of the move is still there
the first hop is 60 board px = 1.5in of a 12in+D6 advance, i.e. a small fraction of the move - the second drag below is shown to ADD to this rather than replace it
the turn step must name the actual rotate keys - {key:rotate_left}/{key:rotate_right} render through KeybindingManager, so an unresolved token would read '{key:rotate_left}' and fail this
the wagon enters the step un-rotated, so the delta the step's done-leaf watches for is unambiguous

second hop AND the rotation in one grab: Q only rotates a model that is currently held (MovementController clears selected_model on drop), which is exactly what the step tells the player to do - grab, hold, tap Q/E, let go

steps.script:
var u = GameState.get_unit("U_BATTLEWAGON_T")
return abs(float(u.models[0].get("rotation", 0.0)) + PI / 6.0) < 0.01
steps.comment: two Q taps = -2 * PI/12 = -PI/6 rad (-30 degrees), i.e. the 15-degrees-a-tap the prompt promises

multi-step movement proven: two 1.5in hops read back as 3.0in, so the second drag ADDED to the first instead of replacing it - a replace would still read 1.5in here. This is exactly what step 6's new wording claims
